After the advent of Islam, the Arab traders
brought Islam in the south Asia and Southeast
Asia. The relations between the Arabs and the Indian Subcontinent were smooth.
However, the sea borne trade of the Arabs in the Indian Ocean was threatened when Raja
Dahir allied with the ruler of Makran and Persia against the Muslims It was the first time
when Arabs, during Umayyad dynasty, made serious attempts to conquer Sindh.
ReasonsfortheInvasionof SindhbyArabs
In the oldest chronicles of Arabs' conquest of Sindh,two main reasons are highlighted for
:he invasionof Sindh:
i. The sea pirates raided off the coast of Debal and looted all the valuables and
plundered several ships travelling to Arabia. These pirates also abducted some
innocent women and children. Upon hearing this, Hajaj bin Yusuf, the governor of
Iraq, wrote a letter to Raja Dahir and demanded the recovery of the goods and
Muslim captives.
ii.Hajaj bin Yusuf also demanded the return of the exiled Arab offenders, who.after
murderingthegovernorofMakran,tookrefugein Sindh.
Since no compromise could be reached between Raja Dahir and Hajaj Bin Yusuf tension
continued to increase. At that point, the Governor Hajaj Bin Yusuf decided to launch a
militaryexpeditionunderthecommandof Muhammad BinQasimwithapowerful army
to fight Raja Dahir of Sindh.
ConquestofSindh
Muhammad Bin Qasim travelled all the way to Makran, where he was joined by
many local Jats and Meds. Very importantly, Buddhists welcomed Muhammad Bin Qasim
because they suffered great persecution under Raja Dahir's rule.
